Below is a brief summary of what’s going on and a single patch in components/prism-c.js that will allow C++-style `'`-separators in both integer and floating literals. Essentially the built-in C grammar only knows about `0x…`, `123.45`, `1e+6` etc., so as soon as it hits a `'` it breaks out of the number token and you get the rest treated as a string. To fix it we simply extend every `\d` (and `[a-f]`, and the exponent digits) to also accept `'`, and allow the usual C/C++ suffixes.

### Bug in action
```cpp
auto i = 1'048'576;        // 1 000 000 with single‐quote separators
auto j = 0x10'0000;        // hex with separator
auto k = 0'004'000'000;    // octal with separators
auto l = 1.602'176'565e-19;// float with both decimal and exponent separators
```
Currently Prism’s C/C++ grammar tokenizes the part after the first `'` as a string. We want all of each literal, quotes included, to be one big `number` token.

### Patch

```javascript
### components/prism-c.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    'number': /(?:\b0x(?:[\da-f]+\.?[\da-f]*|\.[\da-f]+)(?:p[+-]?\d+)?|(?:\b\d+\.?\d*|\B\.\d+)(?:e[+-]?\d+)?)[ful]*/i
=======
    'number': /(?:\b0x(?:[\da-f']+\.?[\da-f']*|\.[\da-f']+)(?:p[+-]?[\d']+)?|(?:\b[\d']+\.?[\d']*|\B\.[\d']+)(?:e[+-]?[\d']+)?)[uUlLfF]*/i
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Explanation of the new pieces:

- `[\da-f']` and `[\d']` in place of `\d`/`[a-f]` so that `'` is just another “digit” separator.
- `(?:p[+-]?[\d']+)?` allows hex‐float binary exponents with `'` in them.
- `[uUlLfF]*` covers all of C++’s integer and floating‐point suffixes (U, L, F, etc.).

With this change, `1'000'000`, `0xDEAD'BEEF`, and even `3.14'159e+2'6` will be tokenized entirely as a number.
